span.p: INSIDE one phase subagent — node by node

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
phase_planner
❌ NOT AN AGENT — a planner node
An LLM call with structured output.
NO tools bound, so nothing to select between.
An agent decides WHICH TOOL to call;
this decides WHAT THE EXECUTOR should do next.

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
phase_executor
✅ THIS IS THE AGENT
Built with create_agent. Has an LLM AND bound tools,
and decides which tool to call — the LangChain
classic sense, exactly. The ONLY box in Diagrams 1–4
that satisfies it. One per phase, five in the system.

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
four-layer validation stack
❌ NOT AN AGENT
2b field presence is a plain deterministic function.
2a, 2c, 2d are single LLM calls with no bound tools —
an LLM call is not an agent. 2d is MIDDLEWARE,
which is neither a node nor a tool.

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
gate_review_node
❌ NOT AN AGENT — an interrupt point
Calls interrupt(), presents fields, stops.
No model call at all. Its whole job is to
hand control to a human and wait.

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
gate_apply_node
❌ NOT AN AGENT — a plain function
Applies the Belt's corrections, runs the policy
advisory as a structured diff with NO LLM call,
commits the checkpoint, routes onward.

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
supervisor router
global_planner + global_executor
❌ NOT AN AGENT
Deterministic. No LLM anywhere in it.
Gate-check on gate_passed plus static edges.
Nothing to reason about, so nothing reasons.
'Supervisor' here is the multi-agent ROLE name
for a router — not a claim that it reasons.

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
define / measure / analyse / improve / control subgraph
◆ CALLED A 'PHASE SUBAGENT' — ROLE LABEL ONLY
It is a compiled StateGraph, i.e. a SUBGRAPH.
There is no class, no create_agent call, and no
object named 'subagent' anywhere in the code.
Where §23 says 'subagent', it means 'subgraph'.

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
8 universal tools + 18 computation tools
❌ NOT AGENTS — plain Python functions
The 18 computation tools make no LLM call at all.
Leaf tools are NEVER planner-executor pairs —
this is where the two-level recursion terminates.
